set.body:
ColumnId.apply routes through validateDesignId, which returns Names.sanitize(trimmed, allowDot). sanitize exists to make GENERATED OUTPUT column names R-safe (make.names equivalent). Applying it to a LOOKUP KEY rewrites the key.

Measured:
  ColumnId("my col").value             == "my.col"    (not the input)
  table.contains("my col")             == true
  table.columnEither("my col")         == Right(...)   untyped path finds it
  table.columnById(ColumnId("my col")) == Left(...)    typed path misses it

So the typed, validated path fails exactly where the untyped one succeeds. And the map is not injective:
  ColumnId("a.b").value == ColumnId("a b").value == "a.b"
Two distinct column names collapse to one id — an identifier that cannot distinguish the things it identifies. Same conflation in EventId/ConditionId/FactorId/TermId (TermId("a.b") -> "a_b").

Diagnosis: one function doing two jobs. Parsing an identifier must be injective, total on valid input, and rejecting. Formatting a name for output is lossy by design. Fix: ColumnId.apply validates and PRESERVES; sanitization moves to where output column names are generated (Names). Add a round-trip law: Id(s).map(_.value) == Right(s) for every accepted s.

Blast radius negligible: columnById and its five siblings have exactly one consumer in the repo (design/.../TypedCoreSuite.scala:77). Nothing in production addresses a column by ColumnId, which is why this has never bitten.

Pinned by IdRoundTripProbeSuite. Context: docs/plans/design-hardening.md section 2.1.
set.title: A validated ColumnId can fail to name its own column
